strengths: Novel perspective shifting machine unlearning from parameter-space re-optimization to representation-space transformation via an information bottleneck objective, leading to substantial computational and memory savings.

Tractable variational framework covering two distinct operational settings: standard unlearning (with access to retain and forget data) and zero-shot unlearning (access to forget data only), innovatively leveraging the Neural Collapse phenomenon for the latter.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple standard benchmarks (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny ImageNet) and task setups (class unlearning and 10% random unlearning) against a wide array of relevant baselines.
Extensive efficiency gains, demonstrating up to 750x speed-up and significant reductions in peak GPU memory usage compared to retraining and existing parameter-update approaches.
Thorough ablation studies analyzing the impact of adapter depth and the trade-off hyperparameter beta across datasets and settings.
weaknesses: Privacy and threat model considerations: Because the underlying encoder parameters are frozen and only a downstream adapter mapping is learned, representations prior to the adapter still contain memorized traces of the forget set. The paper should clearly discuss vulnerability under white-box attacks where an adversary has direct access to the encoder activations.

Heuristic variational assumptions: The variational distributions assume isotropic Gaussian distributions with identity covariance ($I_d$), reducing the KL divergence to standard mean squared error. In learned feature spaces, feature variances and correlations vary significantly across dimensions, making this a strong simplifying assumption.

Generalizability beyond standard classification: The zero-shot derivation relies heavily on the Neural Collapse hypothesis and linear classifier weights $w_c$ as semantic anchors. It is unclear how this approach extends to non-classification domains (e.g., self-supervised representations, autoregressive generation, or dense prediction tasks).

MIA discrepancy on random unlearning: In Table 2 on Tiny ImageNet, Rep. Unl. has an MIA accuracy of 80.5% (and 74.0% in ZS) compared to 68.4% for retraining, indicating noticeable residual membership leakage on harder benchmarks.

strengths: High Computational and Memory Efficiency: By restricting the unlearning objective to learning a lightweight adapter (linear or shallow MLP) over penultimate layer representations, the framework avoids costly backpropagation through the full network backbone. This yields substantial empirical speedups (e.g., up to 754x on Tiny ImageNet) and significantly reduces peak GPU memory consumption compared to full parameter-space unlearning.

Creative Zero-Shot Unlearning Strategy: Deriving zero-shot retention and forgetting surrogates using the Neural Collapse phenomenon (using classifier weight vectors as class-conditional latent proxies) is an elegant and practical way to handle unlearning when retain data cannot be accessed.

Extensive Empirical Scope and Ablations: The paper evaluates both class unlearning and random data unlearning across multiple standard benchmarks (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny ImageNet), supported by thorough sensitivity analyses over hyperparameter beta and adapter depth.
weaknesses: Unaddressed Threat Model and Retention in Backbone Weights: The foundational premise of machine unlearning, particularly regarding regulatory compliance (GDPR/CCPA) and data memorization (as cited from Carlini et al. and Melis et al.), is to erase the influence of sensitive samples from the model. Because this method leaves the entire feature encoder frozen and merely prepends an adapter to the final layer, the original parameters still retain the memorized information. Under any white-box audit or feature extraction attack, the adapter can simply be removed or bypassed. The paper does not discuss this fundamental limitation or formalize a black-box threat model.

Centroid Collapse in Forget Loss Formulation: The variational bound in Eq. (16)-(17) and Eq. (20) minimizes the expected squared Euclidean distance between the transformed forget features and the marginal samples or class prototypes. Mathematically, the unconstrained minimizer of this objective simply maps all forget samples to the global centroid. This acts more as an artificial confusion/suppression heuristic than true distribution-matching unlearning.

Significant Privacy Leakage under Membership Inference Attacks: In the random unlearning benchmark (Table 2), the proposed method exhibits noticeably worse MIA defense than Retraining on complex benchmarks (Tiny ImageNet: 80.5% vs. 68.4%; CIFAR-100: 74.0% vs. 67.1%). An MIA of 80.5% indicates that forgotten samples remain highly distinguishable from non-training samples, undermining the privacy claims.

Anomalies in Baseline Configurations: In Table 1, SISA yields a forget accuracy of 58.2% on Tiny ImageNet class unlearning. Because SISA trains isolated sub-models on partitioned data shards and retrains affected shards, it is unexpected that an isolated shard-based model retains 58.2% test accuracy on a removed class. The training and aggregation details for baselines warrant further clarification.
Incomplete Manuscript Details: The 'Code Availability' statement on page 9 is left unfinished with an empty placeholder.

strengths: Novel angle on efficiency: Shifting the focus of unlearning from high-dimensional parameter updates to lightweight transformations in representation space ($f_\phi: \mathcal{Z} \to \mathcal{Z}$) provides an interesting operational perspective for resource-constrained scenarios.

Resource efficiency: By freezing the backbone encoder and training only a lightweight adapter (linear or 1-hidden-layer MLP), the method achieves substantial wall-clock speedups (up to 750x over retraining) and a significantly reduced GPU memory footprint compared to full-network unlearning algorithms.

Creative zero-shot formulation: Leveraging the Neural Collapse phenomenon (using classifier weights $w_c$ as proxy class prototypes) to anchor retain representations without accessing raw retain data is an inventive approach to zero-shot unlearning.

Extensive empirical benchmarking: The authors evaluate across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny ImageNet across both class unlearning and random data unlearning, comparing against numerous standard and zero-shot baselines, supported by detailed ablation studies across hyperparameters and adapter depths.
weaknesses: Fundamental threat model and privacy limitations: Because the backbone encoder $e_\theta$ is frozen and never updated, all statistical traces, memorization, and sensitive feature representations of the forget set $D_f$ remain entirely intact within the network weights. Any white-box auditor, or an adversary with access to model checkpoints or intermediate representations, can trivially bypass $f_\phi$ (or probe $e_\theta$) to recover the forgotten data. Presenting this as machine unlearning to satisfy privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR) without addressing white-box vulnerabilities or defining a restrictive black-box threat model is a critical conceptual omission.

Mathematical invalidity in theoretical formulation: Equation 1 states the retention requirement as $I(Z'; Z \mid X_r) = 0$, accompanied by the claim that this ensures $Z'$ retains all information about $X_r$ in $Z$. This is mathematically incorrect. When the encoder $e_\theta$ is deterministic, $Z = e_\theta(X_r)$, which implies $H(Z \mid X_r) = 0$. Consequently, $I(Z'; Z \mid X_r) = 0$ holds identically for ANY transformation $f_\phi$ (including a trivial constant function that destroys all information). Furthermore, in Appendix A.1 (Equation 22), the term dropped to form the upper bound, $D_{KL}(p_{\theta,\phi}(z' \mid x_r) \parallel r_\theta(z' \mid x_r))$, is identical to the first term under the specified Gaussian parameterization, making the original divergence difference identically zero. The information-theoretic framing appears largely cosmetic over what is fundamentally an MSE consistency loss.

Residual privacy leakage under MIA: In Table 2 (Random Data Unlearning), Representation Unlearning exhibits noticeably higher MIA accuracy than the Retraining gold standard on complex benchmarks (e.g., 80.5% vs. 68.4% on Tiny ImageNet for standard Rep. Unl., and 74.0% vs. 67.1% on CIFAR-100). This indicates that the transformed representations still retain distinguishable signals of membership compared to genuine retraining.

Potentially misleading efficiency comparisons: The speed-ups and memory advantages shown in Figure 4 and Figure 6 compare training a tiny linear map or 1-hidden-layer MLP against full-model retraining and full-network gradient computation methods (e.g., SCRUB, UNSIR, SISA). While efficient, this advantage is a natural consequence of freezing the entire network backbone, rather than an algorithmic optimization of parameter unlearning.

strengths: Principled information-theoretic formulation: The paper formalizes unlearning directly in the latent representation space via mutual information bounds, establishing tractable variational surrogates that cleanly decouple into retention and forgetting objectives.

Clever zero-shot extension via Neural Collapse: By leveraging the geometric properties of Neural Collapse (terminal-phase feature convergence to classifier weights), the authors derive an effective zero-shot unlearning variant that removes data without requiring access to retained samples.

Outstanding computational efficiency: By optimizing a lightweight transformation on the penultimate representation rather than backpropagating through deep parameter spaces, the method achieves up to 757x speedup over retraining and dramatically cuts peak GPU memory usage compared to existing unlearning baselines.

Comprehensive empirical validation: Experiments span three benchmarks (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny ImageNet) across both class unlearning and random sample unlearning, evaluating retain/forget accuracy, Cross-Entropy divergence to exact retraining, RMIA privacy resistance, and extensive ablations (adapter depth, trade-off parameter beta, and Neural Collapse degradation).

Transparent discussion of limitations: The authors explicitly delineate the threat model (black-box/API-level vs. white-box weight inspection), permanent inference overhead, and the reliance on Neural Collapse.
weaknesses: Threat model restriction: Because the base encoder parameters remain unchanged, the model does not achieve true weight-level data erasure. In white-box scenarios or under regulatory definitions where internal weights must be purged, an adversary with access to the upstream weights could still recover forget-set data.

Gaussian assumption simplifies the information-theoretic objective to centroid matching: The assumption of isotropic Gaussian distributions reduces the variational mutual information upper bound to mean squared error distance toward the global centroid. While computationally convenient and effective in practice, this only aligns first moments rather than fully compressing or matching higher-order distribution statistics.

Scope limited to vision classification: The evaluation is confined to standard computer vision benchmarks (ResNet variants on CIFAR and Tiny ImageNet). While promising as a concept, the applicability to other modalities (e.g., autoregressive LLMs, tabular data) remains demonstrated only conceptually in the discussion.

strengths: Clear motivation and intuitive core idea: Operating in representation space via a lightweight transformation rather than modifying millions of network parameters is a conceptually interesting and computationally attractive angle for post-hoc forgetting.

Comprehensive empirical comparison: The paper evaluates across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny ImageNet on both class unlearning and random unlearning, benchmarking against ten existing unlearning baselines spanning multiple paradigms.

Extensive computational and ablation profiling: The manuscript provides thorough analyses of unlearning wall-clock speedups, peak GPU memory utilization, hyperparameter sensitivity across regularization strength and adapter depth, and Neural Collapse diagnostics.

Candid discussion of limitations: The authors explicitly state the boundaries of their approach in Section 5, acknowledging the black-box threat model constraint, runtime inference latency, and dependence on the Neural Collapse hypothesis.
weaknesses: Conceptual and mathematical flaws in the information-theoretic formulation: Equation (1) sets the retain objective as I(Z'; Z | X_r) = 0 and claims this ensures Z' preserves information about X_r. In information theory, conditional mutual information I(Z'; Z | X_r) = 0 denotes conditional independence of Z' and Z given X_r, which is trivially satisfied by any constant transformation Z' = c. Furthermore, for deterministic encoders Z = e_θ(X_r) and mappings Z' = f_ϕ(Z), H(Z | X_r) = 0, so I(Z'; Z | X_r) is identically zero regardless of f_ϕ. Equation (5) yields an MSE identity penalty only because the variational distribution r_θ(z' | x_r) is artificially centered at e_θ(x_r) by construction, rather than derived from maximizing preserved information I(Z'; X_r).

Over-formalization of heuristic objectives: The forget objective in Equation (17) and Equation (20) simply minimizes the Euclidean distance between transformed forget representations and the global sample mean (or prototype centroid). While collapsing forget representations into the global centroid is a reasonable heuristic, framing it as a rigorous variational mutual information minimization is mathematically loose and obscures what the objective fundamentally does.

Fundamental limitation of zero-shot random unlearning: In random data unlearning, forget and retain samples share the exact same class-conditional distributions. In the zero-shot regime (where retain samples are unavailable), the retain loss only anchors the class classifier weights w_c, while the forget loss pushes forget features toward the global centroid. A low-capacity linear or shallow MLP adapter cannot distinguish retain samples from forget samples within the same class cluster without observing them. As shown in Figures 9 and 10, increasing β to achieve actual forgetting inevitably collapses retain utility on those classes, whereas at β = 10^-3 the transformation barely changes representations (e.g., in Table 2, CIFAR-100 zero-shot RMIA is 70.3% vs. 70.5% for pretrained).

Restricted threat model and questionable compliance: Because the encoder backbone weights remain completely unchanged, the model parameters continue to store memorized statistical traces of the forget set. Under white-box auditing, open-source model releases, or regulatory frameworks (e.g., GDPR) that require erasing training data traces from weights, an unlearning method that merely prepends a bypassable adapter to the classifier head does not satisfy true unlearning requirements.

Limited evaluation scale: While the introduction heavily motivates the need for representation-level unlearning by citing the computational bottleneck of large-scale architectures and foundation models, the experiments remain confined to small-scale vision datasets (CIFAR and Tiny ImageNet). Demonstrating efficacy on larger-scale classification (e.g., ImageNet-1K) or autoregressive language models would be essential to substantiate the scalability claims.

strengths: The paper addresses an important practical bottleneck in machine unlearning: the prohibitive computational cost, memory footprint, and optimization instability associated with updating the full parameter space of modern deep networks.

The empirical results demonstrate substantial speed-ups (up to 757x over retraining on Tiny ImageNet) and significantly reduced GPU memory usage compared to full-parameter unlearning baselines, as the backbone network remains entirely frozen.

The use of the Neural Collapse hypothesis to derive zero-shot proxies (using classifier weight vectors as class centroids) is a creative and pragmatic solution for unlearning in the absence of retain data.

The experimental evaluation is extensive, spanning multiple datasets (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny ImageNet), two unlearning paradigms (class unlearning and random unlearning), comparison against a broad set of established baselines, and thorough ablation studies regarding adapter depth, regularizer weighting, and proxy noise degradation.
The authors are transparent about several practical constraints in their limitations section, particularly the white-box vulnerability and inference-time overhead.
weaknesses: Fundamental mathematical flaw in the information-theoretic formulation: In Section 3.3 and Equation 1, the authors define the retention requirement as I(Z'; Z | X_r) = 0, asserting that this condition ensures Z' retains all information about X_r present in Z. This is mathematically incorrect. The quantity I(Z'; Z | X_r) = 0 denotes conditional independence between Z' and Z given X_r. A trivial constant mapping (e.g., Z' = 0) satisfies I(Z'; Z | X_r) = 0 while retaining zero information about X_r. To preserve information about X_r, the correct requirement is sufficiency or information conservation, namely I(Z; X_r | Z') = 0 or I(Z'; X_r) = I(Z; X_r). Minimizing an upper bound on I(Z'; Z | X_r) does not theoretically enforce information retention.

Heuristic objectives dressed in variational bounds: The derived losses ultimately reduce to simple mean-squared error penalties: encouraging f_phi to act as an identity mapping on retain features (Equation 5) or class prototypes (Equation 10), and collapsing forget features toward the global empirical mean representation or classifier weight centroid (Equations 17 and 20). The extensive derivation via mutual information and Jensen's inequality across mismatched mixture variables (Equations 15 and 19) obscures what is essentially a straightforward Euclidean feature-collapse heuristic.

Conceptual tension with the core goals of Machine Unlearning: By freezing the encoder e_theta and training a lightweight downstream adapter f_phi, the underlying network weights remain completely unchanged and continue to encode the forget samples. While the authors discuss this as a 'black-box threat model', true unlearning (e.g., for regulatory compliance like GDPR/CCPA 'right to be forgotten') requires expunging data traces from the model parameters so that weights can be audited or deployed in open/white-box settings. Under black-box access, this method behaves as representation filtering or output steering rather than genuine parameter unlearning.

Inherent limitation in Random Data Unlearning: In random unlearning (where 10% of samples within retained classes must be forgotten), forget and retain samples share the same conditional distributions. For the Standard Setting, the authors use a linear transformation f_phi. A linear map cannot selectively map 10% of points in a cluster to the global mean while acting as the identity on the remaining 90% of points in the same cluster. Consequently, Table 2 shows that Rep. Unl. barely modifies RMIA compared to the pretrained model (e.g., 57.7% vs. 58.0% on CIFAR-10), and Figures 9 and 10 confirm that increasing beta to force forgetting causes immediate utility collapse.

Incomplete baseline comparisons in the representation space: The paper compares its frozen-backbone transformation against methods that fine-tune or re-optimize the entire backbone. A fairer computational and utility comparison would include simpler representation-level baselines, such as fine-tuning only the linear classification head on the retain data/prototypes, or standard linear concept erasure methods (e.g., LEACE) applied directly to class unlearning.
